newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-WORLD CUP CHAMPION COACH LOSES THIRD STRAIGHT WITH STARS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WORLD CUP CHAMPION COACH LOSES THIRD STRAIGHT WITH STARS.

text.p: MetroStars coach Carlos Alberto Parreira's baptism into Major League Soccer continued to be a frustrating experience as his team dropped their third consecutive game of the young season on Saturday.
Parreira, who guided Brazil to an unprecedented fourth World Cup championship in 1994, watched his team lose to defending champion D.C. United with a minute remaining, 2-1.
Bolivian international striker Jaime Moreno broke a 1-1 tie in the 89th minute for United (2-0) after the MetroStars equalised three minutes earlier on a goal by Colombian forward Antony DeAvila.
Defender Eddie Pope, who scored the game-winning goal in the MLS championship game, had given United a a 1-0 lead in the 40th minute.

It was the third close encounter for Parreira and the MetroStars (0-3), who dropped their opener to the San Jose Clash in a shootout two weeks ago and lost in the final minute to the Tampa Bay Mutiny last week.
The Mutiny (2-0) remained atop the Eastern Conference over United by two points after thrashing the New England Revolution (1-1) 4-0 on former coach Thomas Rongen's return to Tampa Bay.

Four players scored against former Italian World Cup goalkeeper Walter Zenga, including Colombian international midfielder Carlos Valderrama, MLS scoring champion Roy Lassiter, who collected his first goal of the season, rookie of the year Steve Ralston and former U.S. Olympian Frankie Hejduk.
Rongen, who directed the Mutiny to a season-best 20-12 mark and the Eastern Conference crown last year, left the team to coach New England, one of two teams that failed to reach the playoffs.
Midfielder Mark Chung snapped a 2-2 deadlock in the 84th minute to lift the Kansas City Wizards (2-0) to a 3-2 victory over the Los Angeles Galaxy (0-2) in Kansas City.

Zimbabwean international Digital Takawira and Preki tallied for Kansas City, the Western Conference leaders, while defender Danny Pena scored one goal and set up Harut Karapetyan's score for Los Angeles, which reached the final after starting last season with a 12-0 mark.

The Colorado Rapids (1-1) avenged last week's 2-1 season-opening loss to the Columbus Crew (1-1) with a 2-0 triumph in Denver as goalkeeper Paul Grafer made five saves to register a whitewash in only his second MLS game.
Former U.S. international forward Roy Wegerle converted a penalty kick and Jamaican national team member Wolde Harris added a spectacular bicycle kick in the second half in his MLS debut.

Mark Santel scored the first goal and created the game-winner by Gerell Elliott off a 35-yard cross in the 67th minute to boost the Dallas Burn (1-1) to a 2-1 win over San Jose (1-2) in Dallas. Troy Dayak scored for the Clash off an Eric Wynalda corner kick.
